author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction updates that visit rather than adding another, meets the same rules as a booking, and returns to the owner's record. The owner's record offers no way into a correction yet.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the form shows that visit's current date and description.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a booked visit, when its correction carries a description and a date later than today, then that visit is updated and the owner's record is shown.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a pet with a booked visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet has no more visits than before.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a blank description, when a correction is submitted, then the form is shown again naming the description, and the stored visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] given a date of today or earlier, when a correction is submitted, then the form is shown again naming the date, and the stored visit is unchanged.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not exist, or one that does not belong to the named pet and owner, is refused.
[REQ-VIS-003] edge case 4: a visit whose date has already passed cannot keep that date when corrected.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, narrowed 2026-09-11; cancellation stays out).

An edit link or any other visible entry point on the owner's record: intake line 1 decision 'the owner detail page gains no edit link in this request'. Deferred, not declined; recorded in PRD Open Questions.
Changing which pet a visit belongs to, or any visit field beyond date and description.
notes: Intake line 1 fixes mechanism for system-design-expert, kept out of the PRD: the route GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, reuse of template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its 'visit' model attribute, redirect to the owner detail page on success. Validation is booking's (description required, date later than today), per the request. Narrow-reading decisions taken by this dispatch, each reversible by a later slice: (1) no confirmation message after a correction is required; any new wording must exist in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002), and the booking message 'Your visit has been booked' must not be reused for a correction; (2) the reused form keeps its existing wording, including its submit label; relabeling is a follow-up; (3) edge case 3 refusal is the narrowest reading of 'updates that visit in place'. The data-driven validation test covers the blank description, today, and a past date (edge case 4). Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: whether a past visit should be correctable without moving its date; whether the owner's record should link to a correction. Follow-up outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for docs/adr/2026-09-11-non-goal-narrow-visit-amendment.md. The 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR's Status line now points to the new ADR.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction follows the pet create/edit seam in the owner feature package; the system-design Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController now carry REQ-VIS-003, and a VisitValidator row is added. Three small adjustments. (1) VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") method branches on an optional visitId path variable, as PetController.findPet does for petId. Absent: a new Visit is added to the pet, as today. Present: the existing visit is reached through Owner.getPet(petId), then a new Pet lookup by visit identity, and refused when absent. (2) The non-future visit-date rule moves out of the booking handler into VisitValidator (architecture-principles Pattern Catalog, Form validator, in force). Re-applying it in the correction handler would add a business rule to a web controller (architecture-principles Design Validation Checklist). Both handlers get it through @Valid. (3) The controller's class-level binder becomes an allow-list of date and description. No new module, dependency, out-of-catalog pattern or architectural ADR. The NG-5 narrowing is recorded by the product expert's non-goal ADR. Symbol claims rest on grep (IDE oracle not connected, weaker basis): PetController.findPet at PetController.java:76, Owner.getPet(Integer) at Owner.java:126, VisitController.loadPetWithVisit at VisitController.java:64, and the date check at VisitController.java:100.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository), correction tests: the real OwnerRepository over the default embedded H2 database, in a @SpringBootTest context with @AutoConfigureMockMvc (testing-principles Mocking Policy: real implementations first). No test-managed transaction wraps the request. Every stored-state assertion re-reads through findById, so it observes the store and not the request's bound instance. New tests add no framework stub. The existing booking tests in VisitControllerTests keep their tolerated Mockito stub.
Framework transport boundary: MockMvc, the sanctioned stand-in (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy), driving real dispatch, binding and validation.
VisitValidator: no boundary crossed. Unit-tested without a Spring context using real Visit instances, a fixed today and BeanPropertyBindingResult errors, mirroring PetValidatorTests.

Binding target for GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: the persisted Visit reached through Owner then Pet, behind an allow-list of date and description. The allow-list sits on the controller's class-level @InitBinder (setAllowedFields date, description; keep the id and *.id disallow). It therefore also covers the Owner a handler receives. The correction handler binds no other type.

Aggregate path Owner -> Pet -> Visit: Pet gains a lookup of one of its visits by identity, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (skip unsaved entries, compare ids). The controller reaches the visit only through this path. OwnerRepository.save(owner) stays the sole write; the cascade merges the corrected visit in place.

Refusal (edge case 3): an unknown visit id, or one not among the named pet's visits, raises the IllegalArgumentException the controller already raises for an unknown owner or pet. It is raised in the model-attribute method, before any binding or save. Its message carries only the ids (security-principles Realization, secret-disclosure row).
Success path: redirect to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} with no flash message. The booking wording 'Your visit has been booked' is not reused (prd-entry narrow-reading 1, REQ-LANG-002).
Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm is reused as is: the form posts to its own URL, th:field prefills date and description, and the heading omits 'New' for a persisted visit.

patterns.description: One @ModelAttribute method serves both create and edit routes, branching on an optional path variable; the visit model attribute adopts the same shape keyed on visitId.
Identity lookup inside the aggregate that skips unsaved entries; the new Pet visit lookup mirrors it.
Validator instantiated per named binder. VisitValidator follows the per-binder instantiation but uses addValidators, not setValidator.
The rule that moves into VisitValidator: field date, error code typeMismatch.visitDate. Both are kept, so the existing booking test and message bundles stay valid.
Unit-test shape for a form validator.

risks.risk: The class-level @ModelAttribute("visit") method runs before every handler and today always adds a new Visit to the pet. Left unchanged on the edit route, save would cascade an extra visit and break 'the pet has no more visits than before'.
risks.mitigation: Branch on the optional visitId path variable (PetController.java:76 pattern) and add a new visit only when visitId is absent. theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAVisitToThePet guards this against the real store (system-design Contracts invariants: visits persist only by cascade from Owner).

risks.risk: dataBinder.setValidator(new VisitValidator(...)) replaces bean validation. That silently drops the @NotBlank description check on booking and correction alike.
risks.mitigation: Register with addValidators on the visit-named binder only (@InitBinder("visit")). A binder-wide registration also fails at runtime: Spring requires every validator to support its binder's target, and the Owner binder would not (system-design Contracts invariants: VisitValidator runs beside bean validation).

risks.risk: A date check inside the correction handler is a fresh business rule in a web controller.
risks.mitigation: The rule lives only in VisitValidator, and neither handler holds it (architecture-principles Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; testing-principles Test Pyramid). Unit boundaries: tomorrow is accepted; today and a past date are rejected on field date with code typeMismatch.visitDate.

risks.risk: If VisitValidator calls LocalDate.now() itself, it depends on ambient state (architecture-principles Design Principles 3).
risks.mitigation: The validator receives today's date as a constructor argument. The controller supplies it per binder from the system clock, beside the existing minVisitDate read, so the controller's existing clock reach does not widen.

risks.risk: A test-managed transaction spanning the MockMvc request makes the bound visit a managed instance. A re-read then returns the mutated object, and 'the stored visit is unchanged' tests the persistence context rather than the store.
risks.mitigation: No @Transactional on the correction tests. Production runs with no request-spanning transaction (system-design Persistence: open-in-view disabled), so the non-transactional test matches it.

risks.risk: Correction tests write to the shared embedded H2 database. Correcting seeded visits would leak state into other tests in the cached context.
risks.mitigation: Each test arranges its own owner, pet and visit through OwnerRepository and registers them for framework-driven cleanup (testing-principles Never Share Mutable Fixtures; Automate Persistent Cleanup).

risks.risk: The allow-list also changes the booking binder.
risks.mitigation: The booking form offers only date and description, so no offered field is lost, and the existing VisitControllerTests stay green unchanged. The allow-list also stops the booking handler's bound Owner from accepting owner fields posted with the visit form (security-principles Realization, mass-assignment row).

notes: The product expert's follow-up is done: docs/adr/README.md now indexes the 2026-09-11 non-goal ADR and marks the 2026-08-08 row as narrowed. Brief follow-up outside this agent's write scope: docs/architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog says non-future-visit-date checks live in controller methods. Once VisitValidator lands, that clause is stale; route it to doc-sync or the brief's owner. The implementer does not edit docs/. Test placement: the prd-entry file_targets name VisitControllerTests.java, but the correction tests go in VisitControllerIntegrationTests.java. They need the real repository, and VisitControllerTests' @WebMvcTest context stubs it. The prd-entry test_names are kept verbatim. The prd-entry notes put blank description, today and a past date in one data-driven validation test (edge case 4). No architectural ADR: every choice applies an in-force catalog pattern or an existing seam. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: The new setAllowedFields allow-list is a security control that no test exercises directly. A correction POST that also carries an out-of-list field (for example `firstName`, or `id` pointing at another visit), followed by a store re-read showing it ignored, would pin the control against a future binder edit.
approved_aspects: Mass assignment (security-principles Realization): the class-level binder now allow-lists fields (VisitController.java diff `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");`) and keeps `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");`. So the correction binds only the two form fields onto the persisted Visit. The form's hidden `petId` input (createOrUpdateVisitForm.html:38 `<input type="hidden" name="petId" th:value="${pet.id}" />`) cannot reach anything. The allow-list also covers the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` both POST handlers bind. Owner has no date or description field (grep of private fields: Person.java:34 `firstName`, :39 `lastName`, Owner.java:53 `address`, :57 `city`, :62 `telephone`, :67 `pets`). This closes the owner-field binding the booking POST allowed before, so it strengthens the baseline.

Ownership and cross-request trust: the visit is reached only through the owner and pet resolved on each request (`Visit visit = pet.getVisit(visitId);` on the aggregate loaded by `owners.findById(ownerId)`). Pet.getVisit skips unsaved visits and compares ids. A visit outside the named owner/pet pair raises IllegalArgumentException in the model-attribute method, before binding or save. VisitControllerIntegrationTests.java:167-176 proves the refusal against the real store with a visit from a different owner, and asserts the foreign visit is unchanged (`assertStoredVisitReads(elsewhere, BOOKED_DATE, BOOKED_DESCRIPTION);`).

No weakened check: the non-future date rule leaves processNewVisitForm (removed `if (visit.getDate() != null && !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()))`) and moves into VisitValidator, registered through `@InitBinder("visit")` with `addValidators`. That binder name matches the default attribute name of the `@Valid Visit visit` parameter on both POST handlers. Bean validation (`@NotBlank` on Visit.java:42) still runs. Both handlers that persist carry `@Valid` and return the form without saving when the BindingResult has errors.

Error disclosure: the new refusal message carries only the three integer path ids (`"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + petId`). error.html:18 renders `th:text="${message}"`, escaped, so no sensitive value and no markup can reach the page. The path variables are typed `int`/`Integer`, so no text input reaches the message.

XSS: the reused form renders through th:field input fragments and th:text. A grep for `utext` across src/main/resources/templates/ returned no match. Added lines contain no th:utext, no query construction (@Query/createQuery/nativeQuery), no process execution, no file I/O, no Jackson type info, and no logging (grep of `^+` lines in scripts/changeset.sh returned no match). Persistence stays OwnerRepository.save through the cascade.

Surface: the new GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit endpoints expose no more than the existing open mutating routes, matching the demonstration baseline (no auth or CSRF, system-design Security Context). GET does not mutate. Open-in-view stays disabled (application.properties:11 `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false`), so a validation failure leaves the detached visit unflushed.
Concurrency: VisitValidator is instantiated per binder with an immutable LocalDate. No shared mutable state is added to the singleton controller.

Secrets: a grep of added lines for password/secret/token/apikey/credential/jdbc:/Bearer hit only docs/system-design.md prose describing environment-supplied datasource credentials. No credential is committed.

Supply chain: build.gradle and the dependency set are unchanged. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (grep -F 'dependencyCheck' build.gradle returned nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind 3.1.5, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Test placement matches the design-block assignment: the non-future-date rule lives in VisitValidator and is unit-tested without a Spring context (VisitValidatorTests.java:44-92, real Visit and BeanPropertyBindingResult, no mocks) — the rule sits below the boundary per testing-principles.md Test Pyramid, and the unit test reaches it there rather than through a framework-booted test.

Controller-level rules (binding, refusal, response shaping) are exercised at the web boundary via the real MockMvc + real OwnerRepository over the embedded H2 database in VisitControllerIntegrationTests.java, matching the design-block's declared integration boundary and testing-principles.md Mocking Policy (real implementations first; MockMvc is the sanctioned transport stand-in per CLAUDE.md).

No new Mockito or other mock-framework usage introduced; grep -F -e 'Mockito' -e 'mock(' -- src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitControllerIntegrationTests.java src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitValidatorTests.java returns no matches.

All 5 declared Done-when tests are present and pass per python3 scripts/grading.py coverage-map --feature REQ-VIS-003 ('Declared tests: 5 of 5 present'); edge case 3 (nonexistent visit id, and visit not belonging to the named pet/owner) is covered by two dedicated tests (theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitNotBelongingToTheNamedPetAndOwner, theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedForAVisitThatDoesNotExist) beyond the PRD's named test_names list; edge case 4 (today/past date cannot be kept on correction) is covered by the rejectedCorrections @ParameterizedTest.
./gradlew test --tests "*Visit*" --info passed (BUILD SUCCESSFUL) confirming the new integration and unit tests are green against the real H2-backed repository.

Test data follows the Three-Tier convention: meaningful values (BOOKED_DATE, CORRECTED_DATE, BOOKED_DESCRIPTION) are role-named, irrelevant values use the ANY_/SOME_ prefix (ANY_FIRST_NAME, ANY_PET_NAME, NO_SUCH_VISIT_ID), and python3 scripts/grading.py conventions-map found no mystery-literal or raw-construction findings needing an autofix in the two new test files.
Cleanup is automated per testing-principles.md (Automate Persistent Cleanup): arrangedOwnerIds is registered at creation and swept in a single @AfterEach, no per-test teardown logic.
AssertJ fluent assertions used throughout (assertThat/extracting/containsExactly); no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue found.
